response:
Diagnosis before proposing:

Generation 7 resolved the key attribution question and produced the archive leader. **BroadQualityHarvest** (fmb **6.38**, alpha **6.2%**, t **5.59**, Sharpe 0.485, coverage 0.121) dominates on both forms of evidence at full coverage. The matched control experiment worked: CashSampleHarvestControl (6.3%, no quality leg) essentially matched QualityAugmentedHarvest (6.9%) on the same restricted sample, so the earlier alpha jump was **mostly the cash-flow subsample, not the accrual channel**. Yet at full coverage the hybrid quality channel clearly added value (5.3% → 6.2%, fmb 5.37 → 6.38). That combination of facts points to a specific new hypothesis: the *fallback* leg — inventory build net of depreciation — may be earning its keep as a **working-capital investment restraint** measure rather than as an earnings-quality measure. Distinguishing those two interpretations is the highest-value remaining experiment.

Other calibrations: dropping the profitability level (QualityRestraintTiltNoLevel) gave a big alpha but destroyed the cross-sectional slope (fmb 1.91), so the level must stay. Organization capital (xrd+xsga tilt) matched the flagship alpha (5.3%) with lower fmb and Sharpe, so it is a viable but not superior intangible definition — worth one test at the best configuration. Peer-relative profitability and breadth-of-restraint were both fine but not improvements, so industry adjustment and extra real-input channels are settled.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: WorkingCapitalRestraintHarvest
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(invt, 1), at))), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The fourth channel in the leading signal works because inventory build is *working-capital investment*, not because it proxies earnings quality: disciplined firms restrain both fixed and working capital, and profitable firms quietly accumulating inventory are expanding in a form the market does not see.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This replaces the hybrid accrual channel with pure inventory investment scaled by assets, holding the other three channels fixed, so its outcome cleanly attributes the generation-7 gain to investment discipline versus accounting quality. It also removes the internal inconsistency of a COALESCE channel whose two branches have different scales, which can pollute cross-sectional ranks.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: UniformAccrualQualityHarvest
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(invt, 1), dp), at))), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: A single, uniformly defined balance-sheet accrual measure — inventory build net of depreciation — captures the credibility of profits for every firm, and a homogeneous definition should rank the cross-section more coherently than a two-branch hybrid.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: BroadQualityHarvest mixes the cash-flow accrual gap for reporters with the balance-sheet proxy for everyone else, so part of its rank dispersion is definitional rather than economic. Comparing this uniform version against both BroadQualityHarvest and Signal 1 pins down whether the depreciation term (maintenance investment) matters or only the inventory term does.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: PersistentRestraintHarvest
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), COALESCE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(invt, 1), dp), at)))), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), 3)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Sustained restraint is more informative than a single year of low spending: firms whose reinvestment has sat below their own historical norm for several consecutive years have made a durable harvesting commitment, whereas one-year dips are cash-timing noise.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The leading signal's Sharpe (0.485) is below the cash-sample variants (0.66), which suggests portfolio turnover and one-year measurement noise in the restraint leg; smoothing the own-history percentile over three years should stabilize portfolio composition and raise both ls_talpha and Sharpe without changing the economics. This is a persistence hypothesis, the one temporal concept in the restraint channel not yet tested.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: PeakProfitHarvestState
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oibdp, at)), 5), COALESCE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(invt, 1), dp), at)))), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Harvesting is a firm-specific state: the strongest candidates are firms whose profitability sits near the top of its own five-year range while reinvestment sits near the bottom of its own range, regardless of where they rank against other firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's biggest single insight was that own-history conditioning of the investment leg escapes the factor-spanned cross-sectional direction; this asks whether the same is true of the profitability leg, which is currently the channel most exposed to RMW. If it holds, the signal becomes almost entirely a within-firm state variable, which would be a substantively different and more clearly mispricing-based construct.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: InternalVsAcquiredIntangibles
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), NEG(GROWTH(ADD(intan, gdwl), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible investment is only underpriced when internally generated: research spending builds unbooked capital the market ignores, whereas rapidly growing acquired intangibles and goodwill represent overpayment for other firms' growth stories and predict underperformance.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive treats the intangible channel as uniformly good, but the earlier organic-versus-inorganic result (negative alpha when acquired intangibles sat in the long-leg construction) suggests the two forms have opposite signs; separating them turns a confound into an additional channel. This is the sharpest remaining economic distinction inside the winning family and directly addresses the "overpriced growth-credited firm" half of the mandate.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: BroadIntangibleQualityHarvest
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), COALESCE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(invt, 1), dp), at)))), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), xsga), ADD(capx, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), xsga))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Defining the intangible tilt over research plus selling and administrative spending extends the mismeasured-capital mechanism to brand- and distribution-intensive firms outside technology and pharmaceuticals, and should therefore work in a broader cross-section.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Organization capital matched the flagship alpha (5.3%) when tested against the three-channel base, so the fair test is whether it also improves the current best four-channel configuration where the quality leg is present. Because SG&A is reported nearly universally, a positive result would make the signal less dependent on R&D disclosure without sacrificing the intangible mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
